candidate.title: cP-RNA-Seq
candidate.scope: The single cP-RNA-Seq (also styled cP-RNA-seq) chemical-selection and library-construction schematic assigned to this card: extracted RNA with three 3′ end classes → CIP → periodate → T4 PNK → adaptor ligation → RT PCR and purify → cDNA. The three strands are end classes in one RNA population, not alternative assays. The isolated cP-highlighted strand is the title icon. This is the schematic-level implementation clarified by the 2016 protocol, ending at the cDNA library; unshown controls, biochemical validation, optional pretreatments, alternative tRNA-ligase assays and sequencing analysis are outside this graph.

states.label: Extracted RNA: three depicted 3′-end classes
features: Purple RNA strands run 5′ at left to 3′ at right; the top class bears a 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate (cP), the middle a linear phosphate (P), and the bottom a hydroxyl (OH). The leftmost isolated cP-highlighted strand is a target icon, not another input branch.
The input is an RNA population, not three separately processed samples. The text describes gel-purified RNA of a chosen length entering the chemical selection; the drawing begins at Extracted RNA.
Starting 5′ ends are not assigned individually in the drawing; the primary paper describes a mixture of 5′-P and 5′-OH for these 3′ classes.

states.label: Purified amplified cDNA library
features: The final strand is labeled cDNA; a blue central insert is flanked by the green and orange adapter-associated regions.
The physical sequencing carrier is amplified cDNA representing selected RNA sequences, rather than RNA retaining a detectable cP group.

The chemical-selection history enriches for RNAs originally bearing a 3′-cP. It does not by itself prove that each recovered RNA had a cP: terminal 2′-O-methylated RNAs can survive periodate without cP.
The paper also reports that RNA modifications that impair reverse transcription can bias representation. Sequencing and downstream analysis are outside the drawn endpoint.

operations.label: CIP phosphatase treatment
operations.description: Treat the extracted RNA mixture with CIP. Remove linear 5′ and 3′ phosphates to yield 5′-OH on all three drawn classes and 3′-OH on the former 3′-P class, while preserving the 3′-cP class.
operations.mechanism: Calf intestine phosphatase (CIP) removes 5′-P and 3′-P but does not remove 3′-cP.
operations.information_effect: The original linear-3′-phosphate and 3′-hydroxyl classes converge to the same chemical substrate for the next selection step; the cP/non-cP distinction is retained.

evidence.locator: Left title icon and Extracted RNA: purple 5′→3′ strands, top pink cP, middle blue P, bottom OH
CIP phosphatase treatment and its output: three 5′ OH ends, retained top 3′ cP, two lower 3′ OH ends

evidence.quote: The CIP treatment is used to remove a P from both the 5′- and 3′-ends of the RNAs, although the state of cP is not changed.

operations.label: Periodate (NaIO4) treatment
operations.description: Treat the CIP-processed population with periodate. Convert the two 3′-OH classes to the damaged X termini, while the 3′-cP class remains intact.
operations.mechanism: Periodate cleaves the exposed terminal ribose cis-diol to generate 2′,3′-dialdehydes that cannot undergo 3′-adapter ligation. The cP protects the terminal group from this reaction.
operations.information_effect: This creates a differential ligation competence based on the starting 3′ end, rather than physically isolating the top strand. Periodate resistance also occurs for terminal ribose modifications that disrupt the diol, so survival is not a unique assay of cP.

operations.label: Kinase (T4 PNK) treatment
operations.description: Treat the CIP- and periodate-processed population with T4 polynucleotide kinase. Add 5′ phosphate to all drawn classes and remove the surviving cP to produce a 3′-OH on the originally cP-containing RNA; the two X termini remain blocked.
operations.mechanism: T4 PNK removes the 3′-cP and phosphorylates 5′-OH ends, producing the 5′-P/3′-OH substrate required for adapter ligation only in the surviving top class of this drawing.
operations.information_effect: The cP itself is removed, while prior selection is retained in the ability of the original cP class to receive both adapters.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Ligate adapters to the treated RNAs. The figure adds a green 5′ adapter to each of the three classes and an orange 3′ adapter only to the top, originally cP-containing RNA. The lower two retain X and lack the 3′ adapter. The two outputs describe molecular fates within the mixture, not a depicted physical separation.
operations.mechanism: The selected top class has the 5′-P and 3′-OH required for the two adapter interfaces. The lower classes retain a blocked 3′ end, so they do not acquire both adapter sites.
operations.information_effect: Adapter flanks connect the surviving RNA sequence to reverse transcription and amplification. A 5′ adapter alone does not admit an RNA into the final amplified library.

operations.label: RT PCR and purify
operations.description: Reverse-transcribe, amplify and purify the RNA molecules bearing both adapters to produce the depicted cDNA library. The broad source block is retained without inventing internal purification or amplification steps.
operations.mechanism: RT-PCR yields amplified cDNA corresponding to the adapter-flanked RNA insert. RNA lacking either adapter is not amplified by this library workflow.
operations.information_effect: The cDNA insert carries sequence information about the selected RNA population for subsequent Illumina sequencing. It reports sequences consistent with the chemical enrichment, not a direct measurement of the removed cP or proof of the RNA-producing nuclease. Periodate-resistant ribose modifications can also enter the library, and RT-impairing modifications can bias recovery.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title and the checked collection page both identify cP-RNA-Seq alone. All five local transformations apply to its depicted route, with the two non-cP end classes retained through ligation as excluded molecular fates. The primary full text describes the same CIP → periodate → T4 PNK → adapter ligation → RT-PCR architecture. SHOT-RNAs are an application/analyte class, not an additional target method; the catalogue kits and the unshown tRNA-ligase comparator do not add workflows.
